title: Remove duplicates by key, keeping the last item for each key
levels: Meets every requirement in the brief
Misses at least one requirement in the brief

cases.rationale: It records the last index of each key and keeps exactly those positions, so the last item per key survives in its original order in a new list.
A dict keeps each key at its first insertion position, so ["a1", "b1", "a2"] returns ["a2", "b1"] instead of ["b1", "a2"], while the pasted log claims the order test passed.
It removes only adjacent duplicates, like uniq, so ["a1", "b1", "a2"] keyed by first letter returns all three items instead of ["b1", "a2"].
A reverse scan keeps the first sighting of each key, which is its last occurrence, and reversing the kept items restores the original order.
